name: Billie Warren
life: “I still remember the word for alley changing across one street.” Monday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Billie takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I translated the printed words. She corrected the name of the crossing in both languages.
appearance: Billie has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for short copper curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Billie grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Billie can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Billie can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To keep both versions of the crossing's name.
family: Morgan Hamada is Billie’s older cousin. Billie puts the kettle on. Morgan chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Winter afloat*, Morgan says, “I built boats before I sold expensive moorings.”
connections: Quinn Carvalho (station interpreter). They turn the printed account into language the witness will actually sign.

reactions.situation: The witness asks to read the page alone
reactions.response: Billie finds a quiet place for the witness and waits without reading over a shoulder.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Billie asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.situation: If invited to an expensive outing
reactions.response: Billie suggests meeting afterward and explains why without asking the others to abandon their plans.
